sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multilingual Customer Inbound Helpdesk and Outbound Tele-Sales BPO

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, Unitary National Jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Hybrid Elements): rooted in the French Napoleonic Code civil and Code de commerce, supplemented by Belgian jurisprudence and modern EU directive integration; a unitary national legal system with no sub-state tax distinction
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 3 April 1996; as amended by Protocol of 20 May 2009)
BLEU-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 4 June 1984; in force 10 September 1986)
Luxembourg-Japan Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (signed 5 March 2012; in force 1 January 2014)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - Freedom of Establishment (Articles 49-55 TFEU)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
EU-United Kingdom Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended by the Laws of 17 July 2008, 11 January 2018, 25 March 2020 and 10 July 2020); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 25 January 2021 on UBO register filings; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 15 June 2016 (SCSp regime, Articles 101-1 to 101-6); CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - public access discontinued following CJEU judgment in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20, Luxembourg Business Registers (22 November 2022); access restricted to Luxembourg supervisory authorities (CSSF, RCS), notaries, lawyers, and obliged financial institutions performing statutory customer due diligence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of the passport of each UBO, proposed manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority (national civil registration or police authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and manager (recent utility invoice or bank statement, not older than 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated banking institution in country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct (criminal record extract) for each proposed manager of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or competent judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country trade registry or chamber of commerce

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank or professional reference letter for each founding partner, confirming identity and commercial reputation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank or regulated financial institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers and authorized signatories against UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU-FINF), OFAC SDN list, and CSSF domestic published sanction lists; 85% fuzzy-match algorithm with documented false-positive adjudication; PEP determination (domestic and foreign) triggers enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds documentation; ongoing transaction monitoring per CSSF Regulation 12-02 and FATF Recommendations 10-12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Societes) online name clearance and e-Registration platform at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are administered in French; the company name must be written in Latin script and be pronounceable in one of the official trilingual systems (French, German or Luxembourgish); non-Latin script names must be fully transliterated into Latin characters, with the transliteration used as the registered legal name; the legal-form suffix 'SCSp' or 'S.C.Sp.' must appear in the name; the name must be distinctive and not misleadingly similar to existing RCS-protected names
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (name element restricted to entities with demonstrable connection to the Grand Duchy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon expiry, the name may be re-reserved through the LBR portal for successive 30-day windows; on rejection, LBR issues written grounds; the applicant may file an administrative objection with the LBR within 15 calendar days of notification; further appeal lies to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber) within 40 days; for sensitive-token refusals, prior authorization from the Ministry of Finance or Ministry of Justice must be obtained before re-filing; parallel immediate submission of an alternative name is the recommended delay-management path

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not fully permissible. Under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies (as amended by the Law of 15 July 2021), a commercial SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg hosted by a Ministry-of-Justice-approved domiciliation agent with physical premises; a mail-only virtual office cannot constitute the statutory registered office. For a remote BPO call center, the licensed domiciliation agent may serve as registered office provided that it can identify the activity, receive official correspondence, and make the statutory records available to RCS/CSSF authorities; no separate operational license is required for the BPO activity itself.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% estimated probability within the first 24 months of registration, driven by CSSF thematic reviews of unregulated MSI/SCSp structures, UBO register completeness campaigns, and periodic inspections of approved domiciliation agents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR corporate name clearance and reservation (single name application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR tariff; approx. EUR 25 per name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of formation of the SCSp (acte de constitution by Luxembourg notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff for partnership formations; approx. EUR 1,800 including disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and electronic RESA publication of the deed and manager appointments
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fees for online registration and RESA insertion; approx. EUR 40-45

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing (declaration of beneficial owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No filing fee under the Law of 13 January 2019; mandatory filing concurrent with RCS registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / licensed domiciliation set-up and first-year service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; approx. EUR 1,000-1,800 for the first annual period

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg legal counsel: drafting of the limited partnership agreement, AML/CDD pack compilation and incorporation coordination
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee market benchmark; approx. EUR 2,100-3,200 dependent on complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and/or consular legalization bundle for origination-country corporate, identity and good-standing documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Apostille section) and relevant consulates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document consular tariff; typical bundle of 5-6 documents; approx. EUR 150-220

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening data setup and initial vetting of UBO/manager list
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market subscription and per-record lookup rate; approx. EUR 100-140

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (the '1915 Law'), Articles 944-1 to 944-24 (SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016); Civil Code Articles 1832-1873 on partnership contracts; Law of 11 January 2019 on the Luxembourg Business Registers; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), attached to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement (contrat de société / association agreement) filed electronically with the RCS via the LBR e-Justice portal, followed by publication of the registration extract in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations); a nominal LBR administrative service charge applies in addition to publication.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory capital applies to an SCSp; limited partners' contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement and are payable as agreed therein; no legal escrow, blocked account, or paid-up capital certification is required for incorporation, although the LPA may contractually require a bank credit advice as a condition to admission.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST WRITTEN RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF THE CORPORATE GENERAL PARTNER OF [SCSp] S.C.Sp. Adopted on [date], the board resolves: (1) The Limited Partnership Agreement dated [date] constituting the Partnership as a société en commandite spéciale under Article 944-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915 is ratified, and the subscription of the initial Limited Partner for EUR [amount] is approved; (2) the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; (3) [Name] is appointed manager (gérant) with full power to administer and represent the Partnership; (4) the manager is authorised to complete RCS and UBO filings, open the Partnership bank account with Wise B2B or a Luxembourg credit institution, and execute all post-formation formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability verification and drafting of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online name reservation module (lbr.lu / e-Justice.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed SCSp name(s) to LBR for availability screening against existing Luxembourg corporate and trade names. Upon clearance, instruct the drafting of the Limited Partnership Agreement in French (or with a certified French translation) identifying the corporate general partner, the limited partner(s), profit-sharing and management provisions, and the Luxembourg registered office. The LPA must be signed by all partners.
required_dossiers: Proposed SCSp name (2-3 alternates)
Identity documents and/or RCS extracts of all partners
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA)
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or domiciliation letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR rejects the name for identity or confusion risk, re-file with an alternative name or apply for reasoned review by the RCS registrar; no additional fee is charged for a substitute name submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement and contribution funding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All partners acting jointly; a Luxembourg notary is required only where the contribution consists of Luxembourg real estate or where notarization is voluntarily elected
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold execution of the LPA by private deed under Article 944-2 of the 1915 Law. After signature, cause the agreed initial capital contribution to be wire-transferred to the Luxembourg bank account of the Partnership opened by the general partner and retain the credit advice. No notarial deed, share capital deposit, or stamp duty is required for a standard SCSp incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed Limited Partnership Agreement
Bank credit advice confirming receipt of contribution
AML/KYC files of partners and beneficial owners
Notarized power of attorney for any signing agent (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a limited partner fails to fund the promised contribution, issue a formal mise en demeure under the LPA; if an execution defect is identified before filing, cure by executing a supplemental amendment deed signed by all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS registration desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application via the e-Justice/LBR portal using the official RCS filing form for partnerships, attaching the signed LPA and all supporting documents. After the registrar validates the legal form and filer identity, the RCS number is assigned and the registration extract is published in the RESA. Registration does not confer legal personality (an SCSp has none) but makes the LPA opposable to third parties and fixes the statutory particulars.
required_dossiers: Completed electronic RCS registration form
Signed original LPA (or notarial copy)
Identity documents of all partners and the appointed gérant
RCS extract of the corporate general partner and its board authorization
Statement of registered office address and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a request for supplementary information or correction, respond in writing by the stated deadline to avoid deemed abandonment; remedy consists of correcting the electronic file and resubmitting within the same proceeding without a new filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration with the ACD and VAT formalities with the AEDT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the Luxembourg national identification number (NIF) for the SCSp by filing the initial registration declaration with the ACD. The SCSp is pass-through eligible: profits are allocated to partners for Luxembourg corporate and municipal income tax purposes unless the entity opts for corporate taxation. Register for VAT with the AEDT only if the remote BPO supplies taxable Luxembourg services; cross-border B2B helpdesk and tele-sales to non-Luxembourg clients generally fall under the B2B place-of-supply/reverse-charge rules.
required_dossiers: RCS extract of the SCSp
Signed LPA and profit-allocation schedule
Identities and tax residence certificates of all partners
Description of the BPO services and target markets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or AEDT queries the transparent tax treatment or VAT status, file a supplementary statement with the partnership allocation schedule and a legal opinion on the activity; administrative decisions are appealable to the Director of the ACD within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer registration with CCSS and municipal/establishment formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); competent Commune; Ministry of the Economy for commercial establishment permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the remote call center hires Luxembourg-based staff, register the general partner as employer with the CCSS via the employer declaration within eight days of the first hiring. If a physical Luxembourg office is opened, file for the autorisation d'établissement through guichet.lu where the commercial activity requires it, and declare the premises to the municipal administration for local business tax and safety purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and bank proof of the Partnership
Lease agreement for registered office/call center premises
Employment contracts and worker identification documents
Fire safety certificate issued by the municipal fire brigade
Structural load certificate for the office floor issued by a licensed engineer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late CCSS registration carries administrative fines and retroactive social contributions; cure by immediate registration and payment. An establishment permit refusal may be challenged by hierarchical appeal to the Minister of the Economy within two months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UBO declaration in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration electronically through the RBE portal identifying every individual who ultimately owns or controls more than 25% of the partnership capital or voting rights or who otherwise controls the general partner; limited partners of the SCSp are reportable UBOs in typical structures.
required_dossiers: Completed RBE electronic declaration form
Identity documents of each beneficial owner
Organizational chart evidencing ownership percentages and control chain
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to file within the statutory deadline attracts administrative fines from EUR 125 to EUR 25,000 and may expose responsible persons to criminal sanctions under the Law of 13 January 2019; remedy is an immediate late filing accompanied by a reasoned mitigation request where the default is excusable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) — Directorate General for Industry and SMEs; municipal authorities for local commercial premises formalities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No activity-specific statutory license applies to the remote multilingual BPO/call-center business; the general establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011 may apply only where a physical commercial establishment is opened in Luxembourg

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category D: office-based call-center/BPO services are not an IPPC-classified installation under the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; no full EIA report or environmental registration is required for remote helpdesk and tele-sales operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or VOC/combustion emissions from BPO office operations; sanitary effluent to municipal sewer per communal network regulations; electronic and office waste handled under the national waste management plan and Law of 21 March 2017 on waste; office noise exposure kept below the Labor Code threshold of 80 dB(A) daily.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificat de prévention incendie) issued by the competent municipal fire brigade for any Luxembourg premises; structural load and floor-safety inspection certificate by a licensed engineer for the operating office; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering workstation ergonomics, electrical safety under the Law of 17 June 1994 as amended, and emergency evacuation signage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; single business portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SCSp must be registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a Luxembourg notary or authorized e-filing via MyGuichet.lu, obtaining a 13-digit national business number (matricule). For VAT purposes, the SCSp must apply to the AEDT via the eCDF / MyGuichet.lu portal, indicating whether it qualifies as a small undertaking below the EUR 35,000 turnover threshold or is required/electing to register for VAT to exercise input VAT deduction or to reflect intra-Community activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by law and is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax or net wealth tax; profits and losses pass through to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement. Hybrid mismatch adjustments may apply under EU ATAD and Luxembourg anti-abuse rules where another jurisdiction characterizes the SCSp as opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover (small-undertaking exemption threshold); registration is mandatory above this amount and may be required for intra-Community acquisitions or certain reverse-charge services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API clearance or digital stamping mandate currently applies in Luxembourg. E-invoicing is permitted under EU Directive 2014/55/EU; B2G e-invoicing to public entities must use PEPPOL formats. Invoices must preserve integrity, authenticity and audit trail, with retention for at least 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For remote BPO/call-center services supplied to non-EU business customers, the place of supply is deemed to be outside Luxembourg, yielding an effective 0% result. Eligibility requires documented proof of the customer's business status and non-EU establishment. For physical exports of goods, zero-rating is available when the goods leave the EU and all export formalities are completed with supporting proof of exit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (EX-A) confirming EU exit
Bill of Lading, CMR, air waybill or equivalent transport evidence
Commercial invoice and underlying service/export contract
Foreign buyer's VAT or business registration certificate / certificate of non-residence
Inward remittance certificate or bank SWIFT evidence of overseas payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating is recharacterized as taxable at the standard 17% VAT rate with default interest and administrative penalties of up to 200% of the evaded tax in cases of bad faith. Criminal sanctions may apply under the Luxembourg General Tax Law, including joint and several liability of managing partners, and the limitation period is extended to ten years in criminal tax fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for credit institution and payment institution supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a core member of the euro area; both current and capital account transactions are fully liberalised under EU law (TFEU Articles 63–66). There are no foreign exchange controls, no restrictions on opening foreign currency accounts, and no approval requirements for remitting dividends, distributions, or return of capital to non-residents, subject only to general anti-money laundering and tax reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion timeline for export proceeds, including BPO service fees received from outside the EU. Currency proceeds may be held in EUR or freely converted, but banks will require supporting invoices and underlying contracts under CSSF AML/CFT transparency standards.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Corporate Account (EUR) with sub-account for USD
Operational Corporate Account and dedicated Escrow Account for investor capital
Operational Account with treasury and FX facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderately viable. EU-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) and fintech payment gateways such as Wise for Business can be used for quick B2B reconciliation and outbound multi-currency vendor payments. However, due to the SCSp's lack of separate legal personality and possible non-EU general partner, many EMIs impose enhanced due diligence and may restrict the account to pass-through transactions. An EMI does not replace a regulated Luxembourg credit institution for escrow, debt, or large-scale FX hedging purposes.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted for SCSp legal persons when the law firm or notary executes an electronic verification via qualified trust service. At least one authorised signatory -- usually the general partner's director or a Luxembourg-based independent agent -- must undergo a video interview and submit a notarised passport copy. For non-EU beneficial owners, physical appearance at a Luxembourg embassy may be waived only if an equivalent regulated EU/UK bank provides a banker's reference and source-of-wealth certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owners residing in high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract, certified passport, 6 months bank statements from the UBO's local bank, sworn affidavit explaining source of wealth, chain-of-funds documents for the initial capital injection, and a detailed ownership chart ending at natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp without a Luxembourg-registered general partner or with opaque fund structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Partnership agreement (unwritten but evidenced by signed deed), CSSF comment or legal opinion confirming no collective investment undertaking status, a written commitment by the general partner to provide annual financial statements and tax returns (Form 100/200), and a list of daily operational payment beneficiaries tied to the BPO contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial purpose of incoming wire from aholding entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreement with the offshore BPO buyer, tax invoice, time-sheet or VoIP/CDR records, payroll register, and SWIFT MT103 field 70 details referencing the invoicing period and PO number.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicion of money laundering via repeated fixed-amount contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution or capital commitment schedule signed by the GP, audited statement of received capital, official tax declaration of net wealth, and evidence of unencumbered source of funds via a licensed notary or accountancy firm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's regulated EU bank into the SCSp operational account in Luxembourg. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'SCSp capital contribution – [legal entity name] – [invoice/reference number]'. Accompany payment with a copy of the signed capital call, financial statements, and beneficial ownership declaration to satisfy the Wire Transfer Regulation (EU) 2015/847. No Luxembourg exchange control approval is required, but the bank may request a letter of comfort to classify the incoming as capital rather than operating income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EU-based vendors in EUR; TARGET2 for large-value EUR settlement; SWIFT MT103 for international wires; SWIFT MT202 for settlement between banks; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) for goods-related ancillary purchases; and standard invoice-message clearing via the target payment rails (Wise B2B API, SWIFT gpi). All disbursements must be matched against an approved BPO cost ledger and corresponding tax invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/PHP OTC forward contracts with a regulated bank or authorised investment firm
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies (e.g., PHP, IDR, THB) when active onshore deliverability is prohibited
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD or EUR/emerging currencies) for long-term treasury matching
FX options (vanilla calls/puts) and structured forwards with an essential hedge rationale on the underlying BPO service contract
Money-market deposits and EUR/USD automated spot sweeps for working capital balancing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) where the SCSp is a filing undertaking
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end (final date 31 July for a 31 December year-end); partner approval within 6 months is required first
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary penalties for late filing up to EUR 5,000; persistent default for 3 consecutive financial years exposes the entity to RCS administrative strike-off after formal notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual anniversary form; initial declaration at registration and any material change in beneficial ownership within 1 month of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment where the omission is deliberate; refusal to supply data can also suspend registration and prevent notarized acts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership income/result declaration (société de personnes transparent return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the year following the tax year-end, or the extended date notified in the individual filing request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to EUR 1,000, monthly late interest of 1.5% on any tax ultimately assessed, and penal reassessment in cases of non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory audit required when at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average headcount of 50 employees. An SCSp is a non-personality partnership and is generally not subject to the statutory audit apparatus unless its partnership agreement, a shareholder requirement, or the Luxembourg derogation regime triggers appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts; EU-endorsed IFRS remains available for consolidated or voluntarily aligned reporting. The SCSp must maintain double-entry accounting records where commercial operations exceed the micro-undertaking exclusions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE does not operate an annual confirmation statement; the SCSp's general partner is responsible for continuous accuracy. Every transfer of partnership interests that changes the ultimate beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within one month of the transaction and reflected in the partnership books and register of partners. The fair-value register audit requires yearly inspection of the register against the latest RBE filings and RCS filings by the registered office agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined effective headline rate (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax at Luxembourg City; municipal rate varies by commune, generally 6%–10%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: no entity-level CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax on allocated BPO profits; partners are taxed according to their residence. The Luxembourg IP box exempts 80% of qualifying IP income (effective tax rate approximately 4.99%); R&D tax credits and the participation exemption regime are available to corporate partners. No time-limited statutory tax holidays.
